Name: goblin.tools
Brief Description: A collection of small, simple, single-task AI tools designed to help neurodivergent people with tasks they find overwhelming or difficult, such as breaking down tasks, estimating time, or simplifying text.
How can it be used for independent livin: The Magic ToDo feature uses AI to break down complex tasks (like cleaning a room or packing a bag) into simple, manageable steps, reducing cognitive overload. Other tools can simplify incoming messages or help formulate polite replies.
Potential barriers: Requires basic reading skills unless paired with a screen reader. The web interface can be slightly text-heavy for some users with severe intellectual disabilities.
Keywords: task management, routine breakdown, text simplifier, neurodivergent, cognitive support
Accessibility option: Simple UI, no ads, focused single-task design
Costs/Monetization: Website is free, Mobile Apps are a low-cost one-time purchase

Name: Voiceitt
Brief Description: An AI-powered speech recognition app designed specifically for people with non-standard speech, converting it into clear speech in real-time or interacting with smart home devices.
How can it be used for independent livin: Allows individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities who also have atypical speech to communicate clearly with others, dictate text, and independently control smart home devices (like lights or TVs) using their own voice.
Potential barriers: Requires an initial training phase where the user must record specific phrases so the AI can learn their unique speech patterns, which might require assistance from a caregiver.
Keywords: speech recognition, non-standard speech, smart home control, communication, accessibility
Accessibility option: Custom voice training, smart home integration, works with dysarthric speech

Name: Seeing AI
Brief Description: A free AI app that narrates the world around you. Designed to assist with visual or reading difficulties, it uses the camera to read text, recognize products, describe scenes, and identify currency.
How can it be used for independent livin: Helps users who struggle with reading or recognizing specific items by speaking text out loud (e.g., reading physical mail, identifying food packages by barcode, or counting money). This promotes independence in daily living tasks and shopping.
Potential barriers: Requires a smartphone camera and the motor skills to point the camera accurately at the text or object. It can be overwhelming if it reads too much information at once.
Keywords: text-to-speech, object recognition, visual assistance, daily living, barcode scanner
